skeleton: starfish standing on its two lower arms, facing the viewer: root on the ground between the lower arm tips; roll (at the starfish's centre: everything hangs on it, so the cartwheel turns about the middle); body with a belly bone carrying the centre; face on the body with eyes, mouth and brows; five arms at their bases on the centre: top, armL/armR (the side arms, which wave), legL/legR (the lower arms it stands on).

sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a cheerful orange starfish character standing on its two lower arms. Draw this exact starfish as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the starfish's middle alone: ONLY the round central disc of the starfish, where its five arms meet — a plump, rounded five-sided shape about as wide as the face area in image 1 — with NO arms at all: each arm is cut off right where it begins, leaving only a short, smooth, rounded bump. A completely blank face — no eyes, no mouth — keep the rosy cheeks.
2. one arm: the arm on the right of image 1 alone, with its bumps and dots, drawn pointing straight down: its wide base at the top, a full rounded edge, tapering to its rounded tip at the bottom.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or another part) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a cheerful orange starfish character standing on its two lower arms; image 2 shows the same starfish cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the starfish's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the starfish in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2.

Draw each piece on its own, spread out in tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
1. the left eye (on the right of image 1) as it is in image 1: a big dark brown eye with a white sparkle, looking a little to the side.
2. the same eye wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, with its white sparkle.
3. the same eye gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line with a few lashes.
4. the same eye closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc.
5. the same eye sad: looking down, its upper lid tilted up towards the middle.
6. the same eye squeezed shut, crying: a tight, creased, downward-curving closed line.
7. the mouth as it is in image 1: a small happy smile line.
8. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh, the inside pink.
9. the mouth open in a small round 'o'.
10. the mouth in a small sad frown.
11. the mouth open in a wobbly crying wail, its corners turned down, the inside pink.
12. one eyebrow: a small, thin, softly curved dark brown line.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: the starfish waves hello and wiggles its arms

pause.shows: the starfish waving its raised arm high, smiling

animations.description: the starfish cartwheels along to the left, turning over and over on its arm tips, then stops upright.
the starfish crouches, jumps up high for joy with all its arms flung out, and lands with a little squash.
the starfish does a happy little dance, swaying from side to side and waving its arms.
the starfish stretches all five arms out long and wide with a big yawn, then settles back down.

pause.shows: the starfish stretched out wide and tall, yawning

animations.description: the starfish twirls right round on the spot.
the starfish laughs and laughs, bouncing with giggles.
the starfish talks, its mouth moving, its arms bobbing a little.
the starfish shakes its head no, its top arm swinging.
the starfish looks one way, then the other, then back.
the starfish shivers and trembles, cold or scared, its arms pulled in.
the starfish cries, its arms drooping, shaking with little sobs.
the starfish gives a big yawn, lets its arms droop and falls asleep, then wakes up, blinks and smiles.

pause.shows: the starfish fast asleep, eyes shut, its arms drooping
